post.description:
Opens a new AI chat session scoped to your developer account. A session is a persistent conversation context — messages sent within it are remembered by the AI. Optionally attach a document to the session to let the AI answer questions about its content.

Sessions remain active until explicitly ended via `POST /v1/sdk/chat/sessions/{sessionId}/end`. An active session can accumulate multiple messages and document attachments.

201.description: Session created. Returns the new session object including `session_id`, `title`, `status`, and `created_at`.

get.description: Returns all chat sessions created under your developer account, ordered by creation date descending. Each session includes its `session_id`, title, status (`active` or `ended`), message count, and timestamps.

200.description: Array of session objects. Empty array if no sessions exist.

post.description:
Sends a user message to the AI within an active chat session and returns the AI's response.

The AI has full context of all prior messages in the session. If a document has been attached to the session via `POST /v1/sdk/chat/sessions/{sessionId}/attach-document`, the AI can answer questions about that document's content.

**Note:** This is a synchronous call — it waits for the LLM response before returning. Average response time is 2–8 seconds depending on message complexity.

201.description: Message sent and AI response received. Returns both the user message record and the AI reply message record.

404.description: Session not found or does not belong to this developer.

post.summary: Send a message in a session

get.description:
Returns the message history for a specific chat session, paginated. Messages are returned in chronological order (oldest first). Each message includes its `role` (`user` or `assistant`), `content`, and `created_at` timestamp.

Use `page` and `size` to paginate through long conversations. Default page size is 50, maximum is 100.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: The session ID returned when the session was created.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Zero-based page index. Defaults to `0`.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Number of messages per page (1–100). Defaults to `50`.

200.description: Paginated message list. Returns `{ data: Message[], total: number, page: number, size: number }`.

404.description: Session not found or does not belong to this developer.

post.description:
Attaches a previously uploaded document to a chat session. Once attached, the AI can reference the document's content when answering questions in subsequent messages.

The document must have been uploaded via `POST /v1/sdk/docs/upload` first. You can attach multiple documents to a single session by calling this endpoint multiple times.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: The session ID to attach the document to.

201.description: Document attached to the session successfully. Returns the updated session record.

404.description: Session or document not found, or neither belongs to this developer.

post.summary: Attach a document to a session

post.description: Marks a chat session as ended. Ended sessions are read-only — you can still retrieve their message history but cannot send new messages. Ending a session frees up any active context resources held by the AI pipeline.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: The session ID to end.

404.description: Session not found, already ended, or does not belong to this developer.

post.description: Uploads a PDF or supported document file to your developer storage. The returned `doc_id` is used in all subsequent operations — filling, polling results, and chat context. Supports PDF, DOCX, and image formats up to 10 MB.

requestBody.description: The document file to upload (PDF, DOCX, or image). Must be sent as multipart/form-data.

file.description: The document file (PDF, DOCX, PNG, JPG). Max 10 MB.

201.description: Document uploaded successfully. Returns the document record including its `doc_id`, filename, MIME type, S3 key, and upload timestamp.

400.description: No file found in the request body.

429.description: Daily rate limit exceeded for this API key.

get.description: Returns all documents uploaded under your developer account, ordered by upload date descending. Each record includes `doc_id`, filename, MIME type, size, upload timestamp, and fill status.

200.description: Array of document metadata records belonging to the authenticated developer.

get.description: Retrieves the metadata for a single document by its `doc_id`. Useful for checking the document's current fill status and storage details before initiating a fill job.

parameters.name: docId
parameters.description: The numeric document ID returned on upload.

200.description: Document metadata including `doc_id`, filename, S3 key, MIME type, and fill status.

404.description: Document not found or does not belong to this developer.

delete.description: Permanently deletes a document and its associated S3 object. This action cannot be undone. Any in-progress fill jobs referencing this document will fail.

parameters.name: docId
parameters.description: The numeric document ID to delete.

404.description: Document not found or does not belong to this developer.

get.description:
Polls the fill pipeline for the result of a fill job. Call this endpoint after uploading a filled-info document via `POST /v1/sdk/docs/upload-filled-info`. The response contains a `status` field:

- `processing` — the AI pipeline is still working; poll again after a few seconds.
- `ready` — filling is complete; a `url` field contains a presigned download link for the filled PDF.
- `failed` — the pipeline encountered an error; check the `error` field for details.

Recommended polling interval: 3–5 seconds. Links expire after 1 hour.

parameters.name: pdfId
parameters.description: The `doc_id` of the original (empty) PDF that was filled.

200.description: Poll result. `status` is one of `processing`, `ready`, or `failed`. When `ready`, a `url` field contains the presigned S3 download link.

404.description: No fill job found for this `pdfId`.

get.description:
Returns a URL for accessing the raw (unfilled) uploaded document.

- `presigned=false` (default) — returns the stored S3 key path.
- `presigned=true` — returns a temporary presigned S3 URL valid for 1 hour, suitable for direct browser download or preview.

parameters.name: docId
parameters.description: The numeric document ID.

parameters.name: presigned
parameters.description: Pass `true` to receive a time-limited presigned S3 download URL. Defaults to `false`.

200.description: Returns `{ url: string }`. When `presigned=true` the URL expires after 1 hour.

404.description: Document not found or does not belong to this developer.

post.description:
Uploads a filled-info JSON/data file and triggers the AI form-filling pipeline against an existing empty PDF.

**Workflow:**
1. Upload the empty PDF template via `POST /v1/sdk/docs/upload` → get `pdf_doc_id`.
2. Prepare a filled-info file (JSON or structured data) containing the values to inject into the form fields.
3. Call this endpoint with the filled-info file and `pdf_doc_id` as a query parameter.
4. Poll `GET /v1/sdk/docs/{pdfId}/result` every 3–5 seconds until `status` is `ready`.
5. Download the filled PDF from the returned presigned URL.

The pipeline is asynchronous — this endpoint returns immediately after queuing the job.

parameters.name: pdf_doc_id
parameters.description: The `doc_id` of the empty PDF template to fill. Must have been uploaded via `POST /v1/sdk/docs/upload` first.

requestBody.description: The filled-info data file (JSON or structured format). Must be sent as multipart/form-data.

file.description: The filled-info file containing field values to inject into the PDF.

201.description: Fill job queued successfully. Returns the fill job record. Poll `GET /v1/sdk/docs/{pdfId}/result` to track progress.

400.description: Missing or invalid `pdf_doc_id`, or no file in request.

404.description: PDF document with the given `pdf_doc_id` not found.

post.summary: Upload filled-info and trigger AI form filling

post.description:
Triggers the AI form-filling pipeline using the output already collected by a chat session — no file upload required.

**Use this when:**
1. You created a chat session via `POST /v1/sdk/chat/sessions`.
2. You attached a PDF to the session via `POST /v1/sdk/chat/sessions/{sessionId}/attach-document`.
3. The user chatted with the AI and provided their form details.
4. Now you want to fill the PDF using what the AI collected.

The pipeline reads the AI's stored output for this session and fills the specified PDF. Poll `GET /v1/sdk/docs/{pdfDocId}/result` every 3–5 seconds until `status` is `ready`, then download the filled PDF from the returned URL.

201.description: Fill job queued. Returns `{ status: 'queued', session_id, pdf_doc_id }`. Poll `GET /v1/sdk/docs/{pdfDocId}/result` for the result.

404.description: PDF document or chat session not found, or neither belongs to this developer.

post.summary: Trigger fill using chat session output

post.description:
Records feedback about an incorrectly filled form field. Use this endpoint to let end-users report problems with the AI's output — for example, a field filled with the wrong value, wrong type, or placed on the wrong page.

This data is used to improve the AI model and is visible in the admin analytics dashboard. You should call this endpoint whenever your application surfaces a 'Report an issue' or 'This is wrong' UI action to end-users.

**Required fields:** `session_id`, `pdf_id`, `error_type`, `field_name`, `field_type`, `page_number`, `feedback`.

**`error_type` values:** `wrong_value`, `wrong_field`, `missing_field`, `extra_field`, `formatting`, `other`.

201.description: Feedback recorded successfully. Returns the created feedback record.

post.summary: Submit user feedback on a fill error

get.description:
Retrieves all feedback submitted under your developer account, with optional filters by session or PDF. Results are paginated and ordered by submission date descending.

Useful for building an admin view of reported issues in your application, or for exporting feedback data for model improvement.

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.description: Filter feedback by a specific chat session ID.

parameters.name: pdf_id
parameters.description: Filter feedback by a specific PDF ID.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number (1-based). Defaults to `1`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of records per page (1–100). Defaults to `20`.

200.description: Paginated feedback list. Returns `{ data: Feedback[], total: number, page: number, limit: number }`.

post.description:
Logs the event of a filled PDF being saved or downloaded by the end-user. This tracks the storage location of each filled version and is used to build the version history retrievable via `GET /v1/sdk/feedback/filled-pdf/history`.

Call this endpoint after the fill pipeline completes and your application has stored or presented the filled PDF to the user. The `filled_pdf_location` should be the S3 key or a URL where the filled PDF is stored.

201.description: Filled PDF event recorded. Returns the created record.

post.summary: Record a filled PDF save event

get.description:
Returns all saved versions of a filled PDF for a specific session and PDF combination, ordered by creation date descending. Each record includes the storage location of the filled PDF version.

Use this to build a version history UI — for example, allowing users to compare different fill attempts or download a previous version.

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.description: The chat session ID associated with the fill job.

parameters.name: pdf_id
parameters.description: The PDF document ID whose fill history to retrieve.

200.description: Array of filled PDF version records, ordered by date descending. Each record contains `filled_pdf_location`, `created_at`, and metadata.

get.description:
Returns paginated notifications for the authenticated developer. Notifications are generated by the AI pipeline to report fill job progress and completion events — for example, when a fill job transitions from `processing` to `ready` or `failed`.

Each notification includes an `event_type`, `status`, `pipeline_id`, `read` flag, and the original event `payload`.

Use this endpoint to build an in-app notification feed or to poll for fill job completion as an alternative to polling `GET /v1/sdk/docs/{pdfId}/result`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number (1-based). Defaults to `1`.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Number of notifications per page (1–100). Defaults to `20`.

200.description: Paginated notification list. Returns `{ data: Notification[], total: number, page: number, pageSize: number, unreadCount: number }`.

get.description: Returns the total number of unread notifications for the authenticated developer. Useful for displaying a badge counter in your UI without fetching the full notification list.

post.description: Marks a single notification as read by its numeric ID. Once marked as read, the notification will no longer be counted in the `unreadCount` returned by `GET /v1/sdk/notifications/unread-count`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The numeric notification ID to mark as read.

201.description: Notification marked as read. Returns the updated notification record.

404.description: Notification not found or does not belong to this developer.

post.description: Marks all unread notifications as read for the authenticated developer in a single operation. Equivalent to calling `POST /v1/sdk/notifications/{id}/read` for every unread notification but more efficient.

201.description: All notifications marked as read. Returns `{ updated: number }` with the count of affected records.

post.description:
Creates a new developer account and automatically generates a default API key pair (`pk_live_xxx` public key + `sk_live_xxx` secret key).

**Important:** The `secret_key` (`sk_live_xxx`) is returned **only once** in this response. Copy and store it immediately in a secure location (e.g. an environment variable or secrets manager). It cannot be retrieved again — if lost, rotate the key via `POST /v1/developers/api-keys/{keyId}/rotate`.

The `public_key` (`pk_live_xxx`) can be used in client-side contexts where it is acceptable to expose the key. Use the `secret_key` only in server-side code.

201.description: Account created. Returns developer profile plus the generated API key pair: `{ developer, apiKey: { key_id, public_key, secret_key, name } }`. The `secret_key` is shown only once.

400.description: Validation error — invalid email, password too short, or missing fields.

409.description: An account with this email already exists.

post.description:
Authenticates with email and password and returns a short-lived JWT (`developer-session` token) for managing API keys via the dashboard endpoints.

**This token is NOT used for SDK API calls.** To call SDK endpoints (documents, chat, feedback, notifications), use your `sk_live_xxx` secret key directly in the `Authorization: Bearer` header.

The session token expires after a short period. Re-login when it expires.

200.description: Login successful. Returns `{ access_token: string, developer: { id, email, display_name } }`.

post.summary: Login and get a dashboard session token

get.description: Returns the profile of the currently authenticated developer including account details and usage stats. Requires a valid `developer-session` token obtained from `POST /v1/developers/login`.

200.description: Returns developer profile: `{ id, email, display_name, created_at, api_key_count }`.

post.description:
Generates a new `pk_live_xxx` / `sk_live_xxx` API key pair under your developer account.

**Important:** The `secret_key` is returned **only once** in this response. Store it immediately in a secure location. It cannot be retrieved again — rotate the key to get a new one.

You can create multiple key pairs (e.g. one per environment: development, staging, production). Use the `name` field to label them.

201.description: API key pair created. Returns `{ key_id, name, public_key, secret_key, created_at }`. The `secret_key` is shown only once.

post.summary: Create a new API key pair

get.description: Returns all API keys belonging to the authenticated developer. Secret keys are masked in this response (shown as `sk_live_***...`). Use this to manage and audit your active keys.

200.description: Array of API key records with secrets masked: `{ key_id, name, public_key, secret_key_preview, created_at, last_used_at }`.

delete.description: Permanently deletes an API key pair. Any active requests using this key will immediately start receiving `401 Unauthorized` responses. This action cannot be undone.

parameters.name: keyId
parameters.description: The `key_id` of the API key to delete.

404.description: API key not found or does not belong to this developer.

post.description:
Generates a new secret key for an existing key pair, immediately invalidating the old secret. The `key_id` and `public_key` remain the same — only the `sk_live_xxx` secret changes.

**Important:** The old secret stops working immediately upon rotation. Update your environment variables with the new secret before rotating in production. The new secret is returned only once.

parameters.name: keyId
parameters.description: The `key_id` of the API key to rotate.

201.description: Key rotated. Returns the new `secret_key`. The previous secret is immediately revoked. Store the new secret now — it will not be shown again.

404.description: API key not found or does not belong to this developer.

info.title: SDK API Reference
info.description: Public SDK API endpoints for third-party integrations

api-key.description: SDK API key — enter your sk_live_xxx or pk_live_xxx key (without the Bearer prefix)

developer-session.description: Developer dashboard JWT — obtain from POST /v1/developers/login

title.description: A human-readable label for this chat session. Useful for identifying sessions in list views or logs. If omitted, the session will have no title.

session_id.description: The ID of the active chat session to send the message to. Obtain this from `POST /v1/sdk/chat/sessions`. The session must be in `active` status — ended sessions reject new messages.

message.description: The message text to send to the AI. The AI will consider all prior messages in the session as context. If a document is attached to the session, the AI can reference its content in its reply.
message.example: What is the deadline field on page 2 of the form?

doc_id.description: The numeric `doc_id` of the document to attach to this session. The document must have been previously uploaded via `POST /v1/sdk/docs/upload`. Once attached, the AI will use the document as context for all subsequent messages in the session.

session_id.description: The ID of the chat session in which the fill error occurred.

pdf_id.description: The ID of the PDF document that was incorrectly filled.

error_type.description: Category of the error. Accepted values: `wrong_value` (field filled with incorrect data), `wrong_field` (value placed in the wrong field), `missing_field` (field was not filled but should have been), `extra_field` (field filled when it should be empty), `formatting` (correct value but wrong format), `other`.

field_name.description: The exact name or label of the form field that was filled incorrectly, as it appears on the PDF.

field_type.description: The type of the form field. Common values: `text`, `checkbox`, `radio`, `date`, `signature`, `dropdown`.

page_number.description: The page number (1-based) of the PDF where the incorrectly filled field appears.

feedback.description: A plain-text description of what was wrong and, if known, what the correct value should have been. This is shown to the admin team for review.
feedback.example: The date was filled as MM/DD/YYYY but the form requires DD/MM/YYYY format.

corners.description: Optional bounding-box corner coordinates of the field on the PDF page, in the format `{ x1, y1, x2, y2 }`. Used for precise field highlighting in the admin review UI.

session_id.description: The ID of the chat session associated with this fill job.

pdf_id.description: The ID of the original (empty) PDF document that was filled.

filled_pdf_location.description: The S3 key or URL where the filled PDF has been stored. This is used to build the version history for this document.

email.description: The email address for the developer account. Used to log in and receive account notifications. Must be unique across all developer accounts.

password.description: Account password. Minimum 8 characters. Store this securely — it cannot be recovered, only reset.

display_name.description: A human-readable display name shown in the developer dashboard and admin panel.

email.description: The email address registered with your developer account.
